hypothesis: interaction, not aggregate quality: does THIS arsenal exploit THESE hitters' specific weaknesses? Team rolling form cannot encode this because it averages over all arsenals a team happened to face.
why_different_from_prior_six: The previous six rejected families all measured aggregate quality and were redundant with team form (corr 0.51-0.59). This one measures interaction and is NOT redundant (corr 0.11-0.15). It fails for a different reason, which is the useful part.

method.problem: batter-vs-specific-pitcher history averages ~1.6 PA per pair - unusable
method.solution: factor the matchup through pitch TYPES, which have usable sample (~120-150 PA per batter-season): matchup = sum_p arsenal_share[p] * batter_xwoba[batter, p, pitcher_hand]
method.shrinkage: empirical-Bayes toward league mean per (family, hand, season), k=60 batted balls. Median batter cell has only ~15 batted balls, so without shrinkage this is a noise generator.
method.handedness: platoon split respected using modal p_throws per pitcher from the pitch data (924 pitchers: 690 R, 234 L). An early version picked whichever hand appeared first, which would have corrupted every score.

data.coverage: 28.6% (2022-2026, limited by cached chunks + hand mapping)

signal_is_real.note: both directional checks positive with correct sign - a favourable matchup produces more runs for the correct team

why_it_failed: EFFECT SIZE, not redundancy and not measurement error. The matchup term moves expected quality by 1 sd = 0.0129 xwOBA = roughly 0.19 runs per game. Margin standard deviation is 4.47 runs. The theoretical maximum correlation such an effect could produce is ~0.042; the observed 0.0595 is already AT or slightly above that ceiling, meaning the measurement is if anything better than expected. It explains 0.35% of margin variance. A 0.06 correlation cannot move a 56%-accurate classifier.
dilution: A starter throws ~90 of ~300 pitches in a game and faces the lineup 2-3 times. Even a perfectly measured starter matchup is diluted by the bullpen, which this does not model. Signal was strongest in high-scoring games (r=0.085) and absent in low-scoring ones (r=0.023), consistent with starters being removed early when struggling.
what_would_be_needed: To be usable this would need either (a) inning-level or first-5-innings markets where the starter's arsenal actually operates undiluted, or (b) bullpen arsenal modeling to cover the remaining ~210 pitches. Both are real extensions, neither is a small change.
kept: scripts/arsenal.py and scripts/matchup_features.py remain in the repo. The arsenal and batter-split tables are the prerequisite for any first-5-innings market work.
